ice_sheet_mass_loss->coastal_inundation_: Water from melting ice sheets raises the sea's starting level. Coastal flooding then depends on local tides, storms, land movement and the people or buildings exposed.
ice_sheet_mass_loss->coastal_erosion: Rising sea levels let waves and storm-driven water reach farther inland. Erosion can increase along coasts made of material that is easily worn away.
ice_sheet_mass_loss->coastal_saltwater_i: Sea-level rise from land-ice loss can push saltwater toward coastal underground freshwater. Pumping, rainwater replenishment and local geology affect how far it moves.
ice_sheet_mass_loss->compound_coastal_fl: Higher sea levels raise the starting point for coastal floods. Damage can be greater when storms, high tides, heavy rain or river floods occur together.
ice_sheet_mass_loss->ice_albedo_feedback: Losing reflective land ice can expose darker surfaces that absorb more sunlight. This can reinforce local warming, depending on what surface is left behind.
ice_sheet_mass_loss->polar_infrastructur: Ice loss and related changes to coasts and frozen ground can threaten polar buildings and transport. The risk is greatest where facilities depend on stable ice or land.
carbon_emission->environ_anomalies: Human greenhouse-gas emissions add to warming and can increase several climate hazards. Whether they contributed to a particular event needs evidence for that hazard and region.
environ_anomalies->extreme_precipitation: Several hazards occurring together can include an episode of very heavy rain. This describes one part of the combined event, rather than saying that the label itself causes rainfall.
environ_anomalies->drought_persistence: Long-lasting drought can be one part of a sequence or combination of climate hazards. Its causes and effects still need to be assessed for the drying region.
environ_anomalies->wet_bulb_heat: Dangerous heat and humidity can occur together with other hazards. The combined category includes this exposure where high temperatures and moist air coincide.
environ_anomalies->tropical_cyclone_rapi: A cyclone that strengthens quickly can be part of a wider sequence of hazards. This applies only in storm-prone regions with suitable ocean and atmospheric conditions.
environ_anomalies->wildfire_regime_shift: Heat and drought can dry vegetation before a fire starts, creating a sequence of connected hazards. Fire still needs burnable material and an ignition source.
environ_anomalies->floodplain_exposure: Repeated heavy rain and flooding can threaten people and buildings on flood-prone land. Exposure depends on what occupies the affected area.
environ_anomalies->heat_related_mortalit: Heat combined with other hazards can increase death risks where people lack protection or health support. Age, illness, housing and opportunities to recover all affect the outcome.
environ_anomalies->waterborne_pathogen_o: Floods and heat can increase contact with contaminated water when water treatment and sanitation fail. Disease risk depends on the germs present and the protection people have.
environ_anomalies->crop_yield_volatility: Heat, drought and heavy rain can damage crops at different stages of growth. Their combined effect on harvests depends on the crop, timing and farm management.
environ_anomalies->food_insecurity: Several hazards can disrupt food production, income and access at the same time. Conflict, inequality and market conditions can make the resulting hardship better or worse.
environ_anomalies->migration: Climate hazards can contribute to people leaving unsafe homes or damaged livelihoods. Social, economic and political conditions also determine who moves and who can recover locally.
environ_anomalies->critical_infrastructu: Heat, floods, fires and storms can strain power, transport and other services. Damage is more likely where design and maintenance do not match the hazards faced.
sea_level_rise->coastal_saltwater_intrus: Higher coastal sea levels can push salty water toward underground freshwater. Pumping, replenishment, geology and connected canals or rivers determine the local response.
nutrient_pollution->anoxic_dead_zones: Extra nitrogen and phosphorus can fuel algae growth. As the algae decay, they may use up enough oxygen to create persistent low-oxygen areas in vulnerable waters.
temp->anoxic_dead_zones: Warmer water holds less oxygen and may mix less. Severe oxygen loss is more likely where extra nutrients and weak circulation already create pressure. Temperature alone does not establish it.
temp->forest_dieback_areas: Warming can add heat and drying stress to forests. Large-scale tree loss depends on other pressures and uncertain local limits, so it cannot be inferred from temperature alone.
drought_persistence->forest_dieback_area: Long water shortages can stop trees moving enough water to survive. Heat, pests, fire injury and the condition of the forest can add to the stress.
wastewater_infrastructure_overflow->wate: Overflowing sewage systems can expose people to water carrying harmful germs. Outbreak risk rises when treatment and sanitation no longer contain that exposure.
flash_flood_regime->waterborne_pathogen_: Sudden floods can contaminate drinking-water facilities and spread harmful germs. Effective treatment and hygiene can prevent exposure from becoming an outbreak.
extreme_precipitation_intensity->rain_on: Heavy, relatively warm rain falling on existing snow can combine rainfall with rapid melting. The extra water can increase flood risk in snow-covered river basins.
drought_persistence->soil_microbial_depl: Long periods of dry soil can damage plants and reduce soil fertility. Microbes and the functions they perform may come under pressure.
fast_fashion->nutrient_pollution: Producing large amounts of short-lived clothing creates more wastewater and waste to manage. Pollution reaching rivers or coasts depends on what that waste contains and how effectively it is treated.
shipping->carbon_emission: Ships release carbon dioxide when they burn marine fuel. The total depends on vessel activity and whether the source covers domestic shipping, international shipping or both.
cement_concrete->carbon_emission: Conventional cement production releases carbon dioxide both from heating raw materials and from the chemical change in limestone. Both sources matter within the production total.
urbanization->cement_concrete: More buildings and infrastructure can increase demand for cement and concrete. Reuse, material-saving design and construction standards can reduce the amount of new material needed.
steel->carbon_emission: Conventional steelmaking releases carbon dioxide from fuels, processing materials and energy use. The amount depends on the production route and which electricity emissions are included.
mining_critical_minerals->resource_deple: More mining, especially of poorer-quality deposits, can require more rock, water and energy for each useful amount of mineral. Recycling and production methods affect the resulting demand for new resources.
food_insecurity->humanitarian_resource_g: More people facing acute hunger increases demand for food assistance. Funding and access limits can leave part of that need unmet.
temp->tundra_shrubification_speeds: A longer Arctic growing season can help some shrubs spread. The response depends on the species, moisture, snow, grazing animals and disturbance.
permafrost_thaw->tundra_shrubification_s: Thawing ground changes drainage, nutrients and the shape of the land. These changes can favour shrubs in some tundra areas, but not everywhere.
wildfire_regime_shift->tundra_shrubifica: Tundra fires change vegetation, soil warmth and frozen-ground conditions. This can alter whether shrubs establish successfully after the disturbance.
plastics_petrochemicals->resource_deplet: Making new plastics uses fossil raw materials, energy, water and other resources. Reuse and recycled inputs can reduce some of the demand for new material.
plastics_petrochemicals->marine_food_web: Plastic entering the sea can expose animals to particles and associated chemicals. Effects on feeding relationships depend on particle type, dose and other environmental stresses.
ozone_formation_pressure->air_pollution_: Conditions that favour ground-level ozone can increase harmful exposure where the necessary gases and people are present. Actual health burden depends on how much pollution people breathe.
ozone_formation_pressure->crop_yield_vol: Ground-level ozone can damage the way sensitive crops use sunlight and grow. Enough exposure can reduce harvests or make them less dependable.
industry_farming->pollinator_colony_coll: Pesticides and a lack of varied flowers or habitat can contribute to losses of pollinating insects or colonies. Parasites, disease, nutrition and weather also matter, so the affected species and exposure need to be identified.
temp->pollinator_colony_collapse: Heat and changing seasonal timing can stress some pollinating insects. Population or colony losses usually involve several pressures, including food, habitat, chemicals and disease.
drought_persistence->surface_water_stora: Long periods of little rain reduce water entering lakes and reservoirs. Storage can fall or become less dependable if withdrawals continue.
temp->surface_water_storage_instability: Warming can increase evaporation and change when snowmelt and river water arrive. This can alter how much surface water remains stored through the year.
temp->talik_expansion: Sustained ground warming can enlarge areas that stay unfrozen within otherwise frozen terrain. Snow, water, soil and plants determine where these areas develop.
talik_expansion->methane: Permanently unfrozen ground can provide places for methane to form or routes for it to escape. Organic material and low-oxygen conditions are needed for this pathway.
water_stress->urban_water_rationing_zone: When reliable water supply cannot meet normal demand, utilities may ask or require people to use less. The restrictions depend on local operating decisions.
drought_persistence->urban_water_rationi: A long drought can reduce a city's source-water supply and lead to restrictions. Storage, transfers, leaks and conservation affect how much use must be limited.
wildfire_regime_shift->wildfire_smoke_ho: More severe or frequent fires can expose nearby or downwind populations to more smoke. Hospital use may rise where that exposure worsens illness.
wildfire_smoke_hospitalization_burden->a: Hospital admissions attributed to wildfire smoke are one measured part of the health effects of polluted air. They do not include every symptom, illness or effect outside hospital care.
acid_rain_deposition->freshwater_ecosyst: Acid entering poorly protected waters can harm sensitive species and release harmful aluminium from surrounding materials. Food webs can change where the water and soil cannot neutralise the acid.
acid_rain_deposition->biodiversity_intac: Repeated acidic pollution can remove sensitive species from waters and nearby land. Effects are greater where soils and water have little ability to neutralise the acid.
acid_rain_deposition->forest_dieback_are: Acidic pollution can wash useful nutrients from soil and make aluminium more available. This can weaken some trees against cold, pests and other stresses, rather than acting as a universal sole cause of forest loss.
deepwater_petroleum_spill_risk->marine_f: A large offshore oil release can harm young animals, contaminate food and damage habitats. Feeding relationships can change within the area reached by the spill.
Large oil spills can harm fish and shellfish or force fishing closures. Longer-term population effects depend on exposure, life stage and recovery.
deepwater_petroleum_spill_risk->biodiver: Oil contamination can harm many species and damage habitats from deep water to shore. The extent of biodiversity loss depends on the spill's reach and the organisms exposed.
road_freight_diesel_lock_in->air_polluti: Diesel freight releases fine particles and other harmful gases. People near busy freight routes can face greater exposure and related heart or lung risks.
semiconductor_fabs->carbon_emission: Chip factories use large amounts of electricity and some heat-trapping process gases. Carbon dioxide from energy use must be distinguished from other greenhouse gases released during manufacture.
steel->resource_depletion: Conventional steelmaking uses large amounts of ore, fuel and other materials. More efficient production and recycled steel can reduce demand for newly extracted resources.
cattle_grazing_overcompaction->topsoil_e: Ground tightly packed by cattle absorbs water less easily and may support fewer plants. Rain can then create more runoff and erosion where slopes and soil are vulnerable.
cattle_grazing_overcompaction->soil_micr: Persistent heavy trampling reduces the spaces that let air, water and roots move through soil. This can damage the habitat used by soil organisms.
ai_data_centers->cooling_water_competiti: Dense computing equipment produces heat that must be removed. Facilities using cooling towers can consume water that other local users also need.
data_centers->carbon_emission: Servers, networking and cooling use electricity whose fossil-fuel share produces carbon dioxide. Fuel burned in on-site backup generators adds direct emissions that should be reported separately.
aviation->carbon_emission: Aircraft release carbon dioxide when they burn jet fuel. The total applies to the flights and fuel use included in the source's accounting.
telecom_backbone->internet_exchange_poin: Long-distance data routes connect network operators to facilities where they exchange traffic. Those facilities depend on the routes remaining available.
telecom_backbone->mobile_wireless_networ: Mobile networks need wider cable and core networks to carry information beyond a local radio mast. A working mast alone does not provide an end-to-end connection.
internet_exchange_points->mobile_wireles: Places where networks connect allow mobile services to exchange traffic with internet and cloud providers. Independent backup connections help keep that exchange available.
internet_exchange_points->critical_infra: A large network exchange can become a shared failure point if power, cooling or route options are limited. Several dependent services may be interrupted together.
telecom_backbone->critical_infrastructur: Failure of major data routes or switching equipment can interrupt communications used by power, water, transport and emergency services. Alternative paths determine how much service continues.
mobile_wireless_networks->critical_infra: Losing mobile masts, connecting cables or backup power can interrupt public warnings and emergency communication. Distributed equipment still needs reliable supporting services.
fracking_wastewater_lakes->water_stress: Poorly managed oil and gas wastewater can contaminate fresh supplies, while extraction also uses water. These pressures matter especially where usable freshwater is already limited.
fracking_wastewater_lakes->freshwater_ec: Spills or poorly contained wastewater can carry salts, metals and other contaminants into streams or groundwater. Aquatic life can be harmed within the area reached by the release.
fracking_wastewater_lakes->biodiversity_: Salty or toxic wastewater reaching surface water can injure organisms and damage habitat. Effects depend on its contents, concentration, movement and the ability of the ecosystem to recover.
pyrocumulonimbus_smoke_injection->aeroso: Some powerful fire clouds carry smoke high into the atmosphere, where particles can remain longer. This adds to the particle layer rather than removing its cooling influence, although different smoke components can have different effects.
pyrocumulonimbus_smoke_injection->temp: Some observed high-altitude smoke events temporarily cooled Earth's surface overall. The result depends on particle type, height, lifetime, clouds and the surface below, so the effect is not always cooling.
trade_wind_weakening->ocean_current_regi: Changes in east-to-west tropical Pacific winds affect how surface water moves and how cold water rises from below. The direction of the wind change determines the response.
agricultural_groundwater_withdrawal->wat: Irrigation pumping can reduce underground reserves when use exceeds replacement from rain, rivers or managed replenishment. Other users then have less dependable water available.
agricultural_groundwater_withdrawal->fre: Farm pumping can intercept groundwater that would otherwise feed springs, streams or wetlands. Connected habitats may lose water during dry periods.
industrial_groundwater_withdrawal->water: Large industrial withdrawals can compete with households, farms and wildlife for slowly replaced groundwater. Persistent use above replenishment reduces available reserves.
industrial_groundwater_withdrawal->fresh: Industrial pumping can reduce groundwater flowing into connected streams and wetlands. Less flow can shrink habitats and worsen water conditions.
municipal_groundwater_withdrawal->water_: Public water supplies can strain groundwater when pumping repeatedly exceeds replenishment. Alternative sources and lower demand can reduce the shortfall.
municipal_groundwater_withdrawal->freshw: Heavy pumping for towns and cities can lower the water supporting connected springs and wetlands. Habitats that depend on that flow may be put at risk.
coastal_groundwater_withdrawal->water_st: Pumping coastal groundwater faster than it is replaced lowers freshwater reserves and pressure. Less usable water may remain available to local users.
coastal_groundwater_withdrawal->freshwat: Coastal pumping can reduce fresh groundwater reaching connected streams and wetlands. These habitats may lose an important water source.
agricultural_nitrogen_application->nutri: Nitrogen applied to fields but not absorbed by crops can wash away or move through soil. It may then pollute rivers, lakes or groundwater.
agricultural_nitrogen_application->anoxi: Extra nutrients from fields can travel downstream and encourage algae growth. Decay can then use up oxygen in vulnerable receiving waters.
industry_farming->agricultural_nitrogen_: Farms seeking high crop output may apply more nitrogen nutrients. Actual use depends on the crop, existing soil fertility and how precisely nutrients are managed.
agricultural_soil_compaction->topsoil_er: Tightly packed soil lets less water soak in and restricts roots. More runoff can carry away topsoil where rainfall and slopes create enough force.
agricultural_soil_compaction->crop_yield: Restricted roots and poor air or water movement make crops less able to cope with very wet or dry conditions. Harvests can become less dependable.
industry_farming->anaerobic_manure_lagoo: Some concentrated livestock farms store liquid manure in lagoons. Whether they use this system depends on farm design and local rules, so livestock concentration alone does not prove a lagoon is present.
anaerobic_manure_lagoon_operation->metha: Liquid manure breaking down without oxygen produces methane. Capturing and using or destroying the gas can reduce how much escapes.
anaerobic_manure_lagoon_operation->nutri: Leaking or overflowing manure stores can send nitrogen and phosphorus into water. Applying the manure to fields at unsuitable times can create another route for losses.
industry_farming->cattle_stocking_densit: More concentrated livestock production can place more cattle in a managed area. Actual density depends on available land and how animals are kept and moved.
cattle_stocking_density->methane: More cattle generally means more total methane from digestion within the herd. Diet and productivity change emissions per animal and per amount of food produced.
coal_power_sulfur_emissions->air_polluti: Sulfur dioxide from coal burning can form fine particles downwind. Exposure to these pollutants can harm the lungs and heart, with controls affecting how much is released.
coal_power_sulfur_emissions->aerosol_coo: Sulfur particles formed after coal burning reflect some sunlight and temporarily mask part of greenhouse warming. They also cause serious air pollution. Reducing them removes some cooling while improving air quality.
humanitarian_access_constraints->food_in: Blocked routes, conflict or restrictions can stop food aid reaching people in crisis. Households may go without adequate food even when supplies exist elsewhere.
humanitarian_access_constraints->emergen: Restricted access delays help and leaves more needs unmet. Responders who can still reach affected places may face growing pressure.
humanitarian_response_funding_shortfall-: Funding cuts can mean food aid reaches fewer people or provides smaller rations. Hunger can worsen among households depending on that support.
Too little funding limits staff, supplies and transport for emergency services. Demand may then exceed what they can deliver.
food_insecurity->humanitarian_surge_dema: More people facing severe hunger increases the need for urgent food, nutrition and delivery support. Response services must expand quickly enough to meet it.
migration->humanitarian_surge_demand: Rapid displacement increases demand for shelter, food, water and health care along routes and at destinations. Local services may struggle to expand as quickly as needs grow.
surface_water_evaporative_loss->water_st: Evaporation removes water from lakes and reservoirs before people or ecosystems can use it. This can worsen shortages in hot or dry river basins.
surface_water_evaporative_loss->freshwat: Water lost from storage can reduce the flow available for rivers and aquatic habitats. Effects depend on whether enough water is still released for the environment.
surface_water_inflow_deficit->water_stre: Persistently low river or reservoir inflow leaves less renewable water for people and ecosystems. Demand can then become harder to meet.
drought_persistence->surface_water_inflo: Long periods of low rain and runoff reduce water entering rivers and reservoirs. Snow and groundwater can delay or soften the effect where enough reserves remain.
surface_water_withdrawal_pressure->water: Taking a large share of available river or lake water increases competition among users. Less remains for other households, farms and the environment.
surface_water_withdrawal_pressure->fresh: Heavy withdrawals can reduce river flows and separate aquatic habitats. Effects are greater when the amount taken is large compared with the natural flow.
surface_water_groundwater_exchange_shift: Changes in pressure between rivers, lakes and groundwater can move water into depleted underground stores or reduce flow back to the surface. This redistributes water and must be assessed across the connected system.
Changes in exchange between groundwater and surface water can alter stream flow and temperature. Connected wetlands and aquatic habitats may lose support or experience different conditions.
urban_distribution_water_loss->water_str: Leaks mean utilities must take more water to deliver the same usable amount. This adds pressure where supplies are limited.
urban_distribution_water_loss->groundwat: Utilities using groundwater may pump extra water to replace what leaks from pipes. Reserves decline faster if replenishment cannot keep up.
urban_hydrologic_supply_shortfall->water: A continuing gap between dependable city water supplies and demand directly indicates a strained system. The size of the gap depends on local sources and operating rules.
drought_persistence->urban_hydrologic_su: A long drought can reduce reservoir inflow, river supply and groundwater replenishment available to a city. The resulting shortfall depends on demand and remaining reserves.
urban_source_water_treatment_constraint-: Water treatment that cannot handle contamination may allow harmful germs to reach users. Outbreak risk depends on actual exposure and whether other protections work.
Insufficient drinking-water treatment can affect homes, hospitals and emergency services together. It becomes a shared weak point for services that need safe water.
urban_water_demand_peak->water_stress: A short burst of high demand can exceed water treatment, pumping or storage capacity. This can happen even when total yearly supply appears sufficient.
urbanization->urban_water_demand_peak: More people and buildings can increase water use at the same time of day. Efficiency, prices, climate and network design affect how large those peaks become.
wildfire_regime_shift->wildfire_smoke_pm: More smoke-producing fires create more opportunities for people to breathe fine particles. Winds, where people live and how they reduce exposure determine the actual amount inhaled.
wildfire_smoke_pm25_exposure->air_pollut: Fine particles breathed during a smoke event can worsen heart and lung health. The assessment applies to the exposed population and time period measured.
wildfire_regime_shift->wildfire_smoke_ex: Longer fire seasons or repeated fires can keep smoke over communities for longer. Exposure lasts only where the plumes reach people at the stated levels.
wildfire_smoke_exposure_duration->air_po: Longer exposure can increase the amount of smoke breathed and the chance of harm. People with existing health problems may be especially affected.
firn_layer_depletion->ice_sheet_mass_los: The partly compacted snow above glacier ice can store and refreeze meltwater. When it loses empty space or forms impermeable layers, more water runs off and contributes to ice loss.
coastal_inundation_risk->managed_retreat: Repeated or expected coastal floods can make continued protection and rebuilding impractical. Communities may need to consider a planned move that protects residents' rights and livelihoods.
deforestation->pollinator_colony_collaps: Losing forests and other natural habitat removes flowers, nesting sites and shelter used by pollinating insects. This can add to pressures from chemicals, disease and climate rather than acting as the only cause of colony loss.
sea_level_rise->coastal_inundation_risk: Higher sea levels make previously rare coastal water levels easier to reach. Across the assessed tide-gauge locations, relative sea-level rise is projected to make recent extreme still-water levels occur roughly 20–30 times as often by 2050. Local tides, storms and land movement affect the result.
methane_leak_detection->ozone_formation_: Finding and repairing methane leaks reduces a gas that contributes to ground-level ozone over wider areas. Repairs may also reduce other ozone-forming gases released alongside it, with benefits unfolding over different times and regions.
rail_heat_buckling->critical_infrastruct: Hot rails can expand and bend sideways when the track cannot contain the force. Inspections, speed limits or closures can interrupt passenger and freight services, while severe failures can cause derailments.
refrigerant_phase_down->solar_radiation_: Using less powerful heat-trapping cooling gases and preventing leaks reduces their contribution to warming. The benefit is measured against what would happen if those releases continued without controls.
snow_drought->ice_cap_decapitation: Repeated winters with too little snow leave small ice caps with less new ice to replace melting. Their summits and connecting ice can thin until a once-continuous cap breaks apart.
soot_deposition_on_snow->ice_cap_decapit: Soot makes snow and ice absorb more sunlight. Persistent extra melting can help thin and break up an already vulnerable small ice cap.
permafrost_thaw->nunatak_habitat_shrinka: Thawing frozen ground on exposed rocky peaks changes moisture, stability and cold local conditions. Specialised species can lose suitable habitat even as the total area of bare rock grows.
wildfire_regime_shift->thermokarst_expan: Severe northern fires can remove moss, plants and organic soil that insulate frozen ground. Where the ground contains much ice, later thaw can make it sink and form new hollows or ponds.
ocean_current_regime_shift->ice_shelf_gr: Changing ocean currents can bring more warm water beneath floating ice shelves. Extra melting can reduce support and encourage inland retreat where the shape of the seabed makes the ice vulnerable.
snowmelt_timing_shift->nunatak_habitat_s: Earlier snow loss reduces the time that cool, moist patches remain on exposed mountain peaks. Specialised plants and animals may face a longer period of heat and drying.
arctic_oscillation->blocking_pattern_per: Arctic pressure and wind patterns are statistically linked with where persistent weather blocks develop. The relationship depends on the phase and season, rather than being one universal cause.
quasi_biennial_oscillation->jet_stream_v: Alternating winds high above the equator can influence how atmospheric waves and polar winds behave. In some seasons, this changes the likelihood of shifts in the jet stream farther from the equator.
wildfire_regime_shift->permafrost_thaw: Severe northern fires remove insulating vegetation and soil and can darken the surface. Frozen ground beneath the burned area may then thaw faster than comparable unburned ground.
temp->species_range_compression: Warming can make the warm edge of a species' habitat unsuitable. Its overall range shrinks if it cannot establish enough new habitat in cooler places to make up the loss.
gas_power_dependence->fertilizer_price_s: Natural gas is both a raw material and a major cost in making ammonia and urea fertilisers. A sharp gas-price rise can reduce production and raise prices. This is a shared dependence on gas, not an effect of electricity demand alone.
thermal_stratification_intensification->: Stronger separation between surface and deep ocean water can keep nutrients below the sunlit layer. Tiny drifting plants may grow less where they already lack nutrients.
marine_heatwaves->phytoplankton_decline: Marine heatwaves can occur with wind and current changes that bring fewer nutrients to the surface. This can reduce the amount of drifting plant life or change which sizes are most common.
insurance_retreat->managed_retreat_press: Losing affordable insurance can make it harder to stay in or finance an exposed home. Public insurance arrangements may either support a planned move or delay it.
floodplain_exposure->managed_retreat_pre: Repeated flood damage can make buying out, removing or relocating exposed buildings a useful protection option. The choice depends on households' needs and public decisions.
wildfire_regime_shift->particulate_soot_: Incomplete burning in wildfires releases soot and other dark fine particles. Larger or more frequent smoke events increase opportunities for elevated soot downwind, depending on transport.
pesticide_spray_drift_zones->pollinator_: Farm chemicals drifting beyond their target can reach bees directly or through contaminated food brought back to a colony. Colony harm depends on the chemical, dose and exposure, alongside other stresses.
